summary: Aflapin is a proprietary, standardized Boswellia serrata extract enriched in the active boswellic acid AKBA (3-O-acetyl-11-keto-beta-boswellic acid) within a non-volatile boswellia oil matrix to enhance bioavailability. It is used as a nutraceutical for osteoarthritis and joint pain, typically 100 mg once daily. AKBA selectively inhibits 5-lipoxygenase, reducing leukotriene-mediated inflammation, and also lowers cartilage-degrading matrix metalloproteinases; clinical studies report reduced knee pain and stiffness with a good safety profile. It is a dietary supplement and is not an FDA-approved drug.
indications: Symptomatic relief of osteoarthritis (especially knee), reducing joint pain and stiffness and improving physical function
General joint health and management of inflammatory joint discomfort
admin: Take orally, preferably with food, to improve tolerability and absorption
Use consistently; benefit on joint pain and stiffness may build over days to weeks
Use as an adjunct to, not a replacement for, prescribed osteoarthritis therapy unless advised
moa: Aflapin's principal active constituent is AKBA (3-O-acetyl-11-keto-beta-boswellic acid), a selective inhibitor of 5-lipoxygenase (5-LOX), the enzyme that generates pro-inflammatory leukotrienes such as leukotriene B4. By inhibiting 5-LOX (and also reducing COX-2-mediated prostaglandin E2), it lowers inflammatory mediators in the joint. It additionally suppresses cartilage-degrading matrix metalloproteinases (notably MMP-3), helping protect cartilage matrix. The enriched oil matrix increases AKBA bioavailability compared with unmodified boswellia.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to Boswellia serrata or formulation components

preg: Safety in pregnancy has not been established and some traditional sources suggest avoidance. Avoid use during pregnancy unless advised by a clinician.
lact: Safety during breastfeeding has not been established. Avoid use while breastfeeding due to insufficient data.
renal: No specific data in renal impairment; use with general caution.
hepatic: No specific data in hepatic impairment; use with general caution.

pearls: NOT an FDA-approved drug - it is a standardized Boswellia serrata dietary supplement; authored from manufacturer data and published clinical studies
Active principle AKBA selectively inhibits 5-lipoxygenase (leukotriene pathway), distinct from NSAID COX inhibition
Oil-matrix formulation improves AKBA bioavailability over plain boswellia extracts
Also reduces cartilage-degrading MMP-3, suggesting a chondroprotective component
Generally well tolerated; effects build over days to weeks and may allow lower NSAID use
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the usual schedule. Do not double the dose.
overdose: Overdose data are limited. Excess intake may cause gastrointestinal upset. Manage supportively; there is no specific antidote.
